'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[2021 Daraa clashes]]
***Eight [[Syrian soldier]]s, seven [[Syrian rebels|rebel]] fighters and eight civilians are killed in clashes in [[Daraa Governorate]]. [https://www.syriahr.com/%d8%a8%d8%b7%d9%84%d8%a8-%d8%b1%d9%88%d8%b3%d9%8a-%d9%82%d9%88%d8%a7%d8%aa-%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%86%d8%b8%d8%a7%d9%85-%d8%aa%d8%ac%d8%b1%d9%8a-%d9%85%d9%81%d8%a7%d9%88%d8%b6%d8%a7%d8%aa-%d9%85%d8%b9/443803/ (SOHR)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****A [[U.S. government]] [[watchdog]] charged with monitoring events on the ground says that the [[Afghan government]] will be "fighting for its life" and could fall under the control of the [[Taliban]] once the withdrawal of foreign troops is completed. The report states that Afghan "unprepared forces" are facing an "existential crisis" in response to the increasing Taliban attacks. [https://www.voanews.com/us-afghanistan-troop-withdrawal/afghan-government-facing-existential-crisis (Voice of America)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**Fighting escalates in [[Ethiopia]]'s [[Amhara Region]] as [[Tigray Defense Forces]] (TDF) continue their [[offensive (military)|offensive]]. [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|Federal forces]] as well as [[Amhara people|Amharan]] militiamen are fighting the TDF on three fronts. Clashes are also reported in the [[Afar Region]], to the east, with Ethiopian officials accusing Tigrayan forces of attempting to seize the [[N'Djamena–Djibouti Highway]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-58013100 (BBC News)]
*[[Central African Republic Civil War]]
**The [[United Nations Security Council]] extends an [[arms embargo]] and targeted sanctions on the [[Central African Republic]] for another year. [[China]] was the only UNSC member to abstain from the vote. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-07-29/un-arms-embargo-on-car-extended-for-year-china-abstains (U.S. News and World Report)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[Royal Spanish Academy]] confirms that [[Alfonso de Palencia]]'s dictionary dates from 1492, so it predates [[Antonio de Nebrija]]'s "Latin-Spanish Dictionary" and becomes the earliest known Spanish vocabulary. [https://elpais.com/cultura/2021-07-29/la-rae-sanciona-el-hallazgo-de-un-diccionario-anterior-al-de-nebrija.html (''El País'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 wildfire season]]
**[[2021 California wildfires]]
***The [[Dixie Fire]] grows to 221,504 [[acre]]s, making it the 13th largest [[wildfire]] in [[California]]. [https://www.sfgate.com/california-wildfires/article/Dixie-Fire-damage-map-Indian-Falls-Rich-Bar-16345770.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]
**[[2021 Turkish wildfires]]
***Three people are killed and 58 more injured during multiple simultaneous wildfires in [[Manavgat]], [[Antalya Province|Antalya]]. The fires cause mass evacuations in several provinces. [https://apnews.com/article/lifestyle-middle-east-europe-fires-turkey-221b65f565f878f8e547b980dc72759a (AP)]
*[[Flash flood]]ing kills at least 60 people and leaves several others missing in [[Kamdesh]], [[Afghanistan]], amid torrential rains. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58017439 (BBC News)]
*A huge fire destroys part of the [[Cinemateca Brasileira]], in São Paulo, that have the largest collection of "moving image" in Latin America. [https://www.efe.com/efe/english/world/fire-rips-through-brazil-film-archive-warehouse/50000262-4598393 (EFE)]
'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kerala]]
*****[[Kerala]] announces a total weekend [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] on July 31 and August 1 due to an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/covid19-surge-in-kerala-weekend-lockdown-declared-centre-to-send-6-member-team-101627534166983.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Israel]]
*****[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Naftali Bennett]] announces that a booster shot will be offered for people aged 60, making [[Israel]] the first country to do so. [https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-health-israel-coronavirus-pandemic-775e772a7507bcab708e9eea4bdcc50a (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Tokyo]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 3,865 new cases of COVID-19, while the number of new cases across [[Japan]] surpasses 10,000 for the first time. [https://www.asahi.com/sp/ajw/articles/14406423 (''The Asahi Shimbun'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] announces that they will ban air travel for unvaccinated people, as well as entry to schools for both staff and students over the age of 18 beginning on August 1 and will also require public sector workers, public transport workers and retail staff to get vaccinated beginning on August 31 or risk a ban on entry to shopping malls, restaurants, and government offices. [https://www.usnews.com/news/top-news/articles/2021-07-29/pakistan-to-ban-public-sector-education-malls-air-travel-for-unvaccinated (U.S. News and World Report)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 17,669 new cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 561,030. The country also reports a record 165 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 4,562. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/thailand-reports-daily-record-of-17669-covid-19-cases (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan]]
****[[Uzbekistan]] reports a record 879 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 127,506. [https://m.akipress.com/news:661008:Uzbekistan_records_879_new_coronavirus_and_529_pneumonia_cases/ (AKIPress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****[[Northern Ireland]] announces that it will allow fully-vaccinated travellers from amber list [[European Union]] countries as well as the [[United States]] to enter without needing to [[quarantine]] beginning on August 1. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/jul/29/northern-ireland-to-allow-double-jabbed-us-and-eu-visitors-without-quarantine (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] announces three phases for lifting its COVID-19-related restrictions, including ending localized curfews and operating hours restrictions for restaurants, stores and cultural venues on August 1 as the number of cases continues to decline. However, bars and discos will only be allowed to reopen in October. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/Health/wireStory/portugal-eases-virus-limits-takes-aim-total-freedom-79145550 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 799 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours for the third time in a month, bringing the nationwide death toll to 156,277. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/07/29/russia-reports-record-coronavirus-deaths-record-for-3rd-time-a74645/ (''The Moscow Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] announces that federal employees will be [[COVID-19 vaccine mandates in the United States|required]] to receive a COVID-19 vaccine or undergo a [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test]]. He also urges [[The Pentagon]] to approve a [[COVID-19 vaccine mandates in the United States|COVID-19 vaccine mandate]] for the [[United States Armed Forces|United States military]]. [https://www.businessinsider.com/biden-all-federal-employees-must-be-vaccinated-or-tested-2021-7 (Business Insider)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Arkansas]]
****[[Governor of Arkansas|Arkansas Governor]] [[Asa Hutchinson]] declares a public health emergency in [[Arkansas]] amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. He also announces a special legislative session to change the law that prevents public schools from issuing [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandates]]. [https://katv.com/news/local/arkansas-governor-to-hold-news-conference-as-covid-19-cases-surge (KATV-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vermont]]
****[[Vermont]] becomes the first [[U.S. state]] to [[vaccination|vaccinate]] 70% of people aged 12 to 17. [https://www.necn.com/news/coronavirus/vermont-is-the-first-state-to-vaccinate-70-of-eligible-kids-against-covid-19/2519572/ (NECN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
****[[Washington, D.C.|Washington D.C.]] [[Mayor of Washington D.C.|Mayor]] [[Muriel Bowser]] issues a [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] for indoor public spaces as part of an effort to reduce the spread of COVID-19. The mandate will be in effect on July 31. [https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/565465-dc-brings-back-indoor-mask-mandate-starting-saturday (''The Hill'')]
**Over 4 billion doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] has been administered worldwide. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-07-billion-anti-covid-shots-worldwide.html (Medical Xpress)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[LGBT rights in Uganda]]
**Local [[human rights in Uganda|human rights]] activists in [[Uganda]] petition President [[Yoweri Museveni]] not to sign a controversial bill against [[gay sex]] into law as it could increase [[discrimination]] and [[hate crime]]s and incite violence against gay men. The bill further criminalizes [[homosexuality]] by punishing "penetration of another person’s [[anus]]" with up to 10 years' imprisonment. Richard Lusimbo, a 34-year-old activist, says that even people suspected of being gay will be attacked if the bill comes into effect. [https://www.pmldaily.com/news/2021/07/anti-gay-legislation-sparks-controversy-and-fear.html (''PML Daily'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Peru]]'s [[President of Peru|President]] [[Pedro Castillo]] names [[Guido Bellido]] of the party [[Free Peru]] as his [[Prime Minister of Peru|prime minister]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/peru-president-castillo-names-member-far-left-party-prime-minister-2021-07-29/ (Reuters)]

**[[San Marino at the 2020 Summer Olympics]], [[Shooting at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
